    Compute — a cloud-masked NDVI pipeline over Lake Tahoe¶

    You compose library operators into a cloud-masked NDVI pipeline, then add one operator of your own. This is step 3 of the Lake Tahoe story. The find notebook chose the scene, 2024-09-22; the cut notebook chose the 10 km South Shore box used here.

    How Sequential and Graph work is explained once in Operator concepts. Here you use them on real pixels.

    What you'll learn:

    1. Chain library operators with | into a Sequential.
    2. Mask cloud and shadow with gz.S2SCL and gz.ApplyMask.
    3. Wire a two-branch pipeline as a Graph.
    4. Compute several indices from one input with gz.Fanout.
    5. Write your own operator and check it with geotoolz.testing.check_operator.

    1. Load the South Shore box through the catalog¶

    The scene comes from the same catalog search as the other two notebooks. Load green, red and NIR at their native 10 m, plus the 20 m scene classification layer (SCL). SCL holds class labels, so it is upsampled with nearest-neighbour resampling.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    client: pystac_client.Client = pystac_client.Client.open(
    "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1",
    modifier=planetary_computer.sign_inplace,
)
catalog: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.sources.from_stac_search(
    client,
    collections=["sentinel-2-l2a"],
    bounds=(-120.25, 38.85, -119.85, 39.30),  # Lake Tahoe, lon/lat
    datetime="2024-09-22",
    asset_key="*",
).where("crs == 'EPSG:32610'")  # the UTM zone 10 tile covers the box
day: pd.Timestamp = pd.Timestamp("2024-09-22")
south_shore: gc.GeoSlice = gc.GeoSlice(
    bounds=(755e3, 4308e3, 765e3, 4318e3),  # UTM 10N, m
    interval=pd.Interval(day, day + pd.Timedelta(hours=23, minutes=59), closed="both"),
    resolution=(10.0, 10.0),
    crs="EPSG:32610",
)


def load(asset: str, resampling: Resampling = Resampling.bilinear) -> GeoTensor:
    """Read one asset of the scene on the South Shore grid."""
    rows: gc.GeoCatalog = catalog.where(f"asset_key == '{asset}'")
    return gc.load.load_raster(rows, south_shore, resampling=resampling)


GREEN, RED, NIR, QA = 0, 1, 2, 3  # band positions in the stack below
green: GeoTensor = load("B03")  # (1, 1000, 1000) uint16
red: GeoTensor = load("B04")  # (1, 1000, 1000) uint16
nir: GeoTensor = load("B08")  # (1, 1000, 1000) uint16
scl: GeoTensor = load("SCL", Resampling.nearest)  # (1, 1000, 1000) uint8, 20 m → 10 m
scene: GeoTensor = gz.StackBands()([green, red, nir, scl])  # (4, 1000, 1000) uint16
print(f"scene: {scene.shape} {scene.dtype}, crs={scene.crs}")

    2. Chain operators with Sequential¶

    a | b builds a Sequential that runs a, then b. Keep the three reflectance bands, decode the stored values (reflectance × 10 000) with gz.DNToReflectance, then compute gz.NDVI.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    keep: gz.SelectBands = gz.SelectBands(bands=[GREEN, RED, NIR])
reflectance: gz.Sequential = keep | gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4)
ndvi_pipe: gz.Sequential = reflectance | gz.NDVI(red=RED, nir=NIR)
ndvi: GeoTensor = ndvi_pipe(scene)  # (4, 1000, 1000) uint16 → (1000, 1000) float64
print(ndvi_pipe)
print(
    f"ndvi: {ndvi.shape} {ndvi.dtype}, range [{np.nanmin(ndvi):.2f}, {np.nanmax(ndvi):.2f}]"
)
    keep: gz.SelectBands = gz.SelectBands(bands=[GREEN, RED, NIR]) reflectance: gz.Sequential = keep | gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4) ndvi_pipe: gz.Sequential = reflectance | gz.NDVI(red=RED, nir=NIR) ndvi: GeoTensor = ndvi_pipe(scene) # (4, 1000, 1000) uint16 → (1000, 1000) float64 print(ndvi_pipe) print( f"ndvi: {ndvi.shape} {ndvi.dtype}, range [{np.nanmin(ndvi):.2f}, {np.nanmax(ndvi):.2f}]" )
    Sequential([SelectBands(bands=[0, 1, 2], axis=-3), DNToReflectance(scale=0.0001, offset=0.0, axis=-3), NDVI(red=1, nir=2, axis=-3, eps=1e-10)])
ndvi: (1000, 1000) float64, range [-0.27, 0.72]

    3. Build a cloud mask from SCL¶

    gz.S2SCL returns a boolean mask where True means drop the pixel, the polarity every geotoolz mask uses (see Mask polarity). By default it drops every class except vegetation, bare soil and water.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    scl_mask: gz.S2SCL = gz.S2SCL(qa_band=QA)
drop: GeoTensor = scl_mask(scene)  # (4, 1000, 1000) uint16 → (1000, 1000) bool
classes, counts = np.unique(np.asarray(scene)[QA], return_counts=True)
for value, count in zip(classes, counts, strict=True):
    print(f"{gz.SCL(int(value)).name:<15} {count / counts.sum():6.1%}")
print(f"dropped: {np.asarray(drop).mean():.1%} of pixels")
    scl_mask: gz.S2SCL = gz.S2SCL(qa_band=QA) drop: GeoTensor = scl_mask(scene) # (4, 1000, 1000) uint16 → (1000, 1000) bool classes, counts = np.unique(np.asarray(scene)[QA], return_counts=True) for value, count in zip(classes, counts, strict=True): print(f"{gz.SCL(int(value)).name:<15} {count / counts.sum():6.1%}") print(f"dropped: {np.asarray(drop).mean():.1%} of pixels")
    DARK_AREA_PIXELS   0.9%
VEGETATION       48.0%
NOT_VEGETATED    16.2%
WATER            33.2%
UNCLASSIFIED      1.7%
dropped: 2.6% of pixels

    This late-September scene is nearly cloud-free, so the mask mostly drops dark (shaded) and unclassified pixels. No NO_DATA class appears, so the tile covers the whole box.

    4. Wire both branches as a Graph¶

    NDVI and the mask both start from the same scene and meet in gz.ApplyMask. A linear Sequential cannot express that, so call the operators on a symbolic gz.Input and wrap the result in a gz.Graph.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    scene_in: gz.Input = gz.Input("scene")
ndvi_node: gz.Node = ndvi_pipe(scene_in)
drop_node: gz.Node = scl_mask(scene_in)
clean_node: gz.Node = gz.ApplyMask()(ndvi_node, drop_node)  # dropped pixels become NaN
graph: gz.Graph = gz.Graph(
    inputs={"scene": scene_in},
    outputs={"ndvi": ndvi_node, "drop": drop_node, "clean": clean_node},
)
out: dict[str, GeoTensor] = graph(scene=scene)
print({name: (value.shape, str(value.dtype)) for name, value in out.items()})
    scene_in: gz.Input = gz.Input("scene") ndvi_node: gz.Node = ndvi_pipe(scene_in) drop_node: gz.Node = scl_mask(scene_in) clean_node: gz.Node = gz.ApplyMask()(ndvi_node, drop_node) # dropped pixels become NaN graph: gz.Graph = gz.Graph( inputs={"scene": scene_in}, outputs={"ndvi": ndvi_node, "drop": drop_node, "clean": clean_node}, ) out: dict[str, GeoTensor] = graph(scene=scene) print({name: (value.shape, str(value.dtype)) for name, value in out.items()})
    {'ndvi': ((1000, 1000), 'float64'), 'drop': ((1000, 1000), 'bool'), 'clean': ((1000, 1000), 'float64')}

    5. Several indices from one input with Fanout¶

    gz.Fanout runs each named operator on the same input and returns a dict. Here it adds the McFeeters water index, gz.NDWI, which uses the green band. Water has NDWI above 0, so NDWI > 0 should agree with SCL's own WATER class.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    ndvi_op: gz.NDVI = gz.NDVI(red=RED, nir=NIR)
ndwi_op: gz.NDWI = gz.NDWI(green=GREEN, nir=NIR)
indices: gz.Fanout = gz.Fanout({"ndvi": ndvi_op, "ndwi": ndwi_op})
fan: gz.Sequential = reflectance | indices
products: dict[str, GeoTensor] = fan(scene)  # {name: (1000, 1000) float64}
ndwi_water: np.ndarray = np.asarray(products["ndwi"]) > 0  # (1000, 1000) bool
scl_water: np.ndarray = np.asarray(scene)[QA] == gz.SCL.WATER  # (1000, 1000) bool
agree: float = (ndwi_water == scl_water).mean()
print(
    f"water: NDWI {ndwi_water.mean():.1%}, SCL {scl_water.mean():.1%}; agree {agree:.1%}"
)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))
for ax, title, img in zip(
    axes, ("NDWI > 0", "SCL class WATER"), (ndwi_water, scl_water), strict=True
):
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="Blues", interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()
    ndvi_op: gz.NDVI = gz.NDVI(red=RED, nir=NIR) ndwi_op: gz.NDWI = gz.NDWI(green=GREEN, nir=NIR) indices: gz.Fanout = gz.Fanout({"ndvi": ndvi_op, "ndwi": ndwi_op}) fan: gz.Sequential = reflectance | indices products: dict[str, GeoTensor] = fan(scene) # {name: (1000, 1000) float64} ndwi_water: np.ndarray = np.asarray(products["ndwi"]) > 0 # (1000, 1000) bool scl_water: np.ndarray = np.asarray(scene)[QA] == gz.SCL.WATER # (1000, 1000) bool agree: float = (ndwi_water == scl_water).mean() print( f"water: NDWI {ndwi_water.mean():.1%}, SCL {scl_water.mean():.1%}; agree {agree:.1%}" ) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5)) for ax, title, img in zip( axes, ("NDWI > 0", "SCL class WATER"), (ndwi_water, scl_water), strict=True ): ax.imshow(img, cmap="Blues", interpolation="nearest") ax.set_title(title) ax.set_xticks([]) ax.set_yticks([]) plt.show()
    water: NDWI 33.1%, SCL 33.2%; agree 98.9%

    6. Write your own operator¶

    The library has no NDVI land-cover classifier, so write one. Subclass gz.Operator, take keyword-only configuration, and put the work in _apply; never override __call__. Rewrap the result with geotoolz.carrier.wrap_like, which keeps the georeferencing and sets the new fill.

    The full walkthrough is Define an operator.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    class NDVIClasses(gz.Operator):
    """Label NDVI as water (1), sparse cover (2) or vegetation (3); 0 = no data.

    Args:
        water_below: NDVI under this value is water.
        vegetation_above: NDVI at or above this value is vegetation.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, water_below: float = 0.02, vegetation_above: float = 0.25):
        self.water_below = water_below
        self.vegetation_above = vegetation_above

    def _apply(self, ndvi: GeoTensor) -> GeoTensor:
        values: np.ndarray = np.asarray(ndvi)  # (..., H, W) float
        edges: list[float] = [self.water_below, self.vegetation_above]
        labels: np.ndarray = np.digitize(values, edges) + 1  # (..., H, W) int64
        labels[~np.isfinite(values)] = 0  # nodata stays nodata
        return wrap_like(ndvi, labels.astype(np.uint8), fill_value_default=0)
    class NDVIClasses(gz.Operator): """Label NDVI as water (1), sparse cover (2) or vegetation (3); 0 = no data. Args: water_below: NDVI under this value is water. vegetation_above: NDVI at or above this value is vegetation. """ def __init__(self, *, water_below: float = 0.02, vegetation_above: float = 0.25): self.water_below = water_below self.vegetation_above = vegetation_above def _apply(self, ndvi: GeoTensor) -> GeoTensor: values: np.ndarray = np.asarray(ndvi) # (..., H, W) float edges: list[float] = [self.water_below, self.vegetation_above] labels: np.ndarray = np.digitize(values, edges) + 1 # (..., H, W) int64 labels[~np.isfinite(values)] = 0 # nodata stays nodata return wrap_like(ndvi, labels.astype(np.uint8), fill_value_default=0)

    Clear lake water sits near NDVI 0 in this scene, so water_below=0.02 separates it from bare granite.

    check_operator runs the library's own contract checks on your operator. They cover config round-trip, graph mode, fresh attrs, dtype-matched fills and (T, C, H, W) stacks. It raises on the first failure.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    classify: NDVIClasses = NDVIClasses(water_below=0.02, vegetation_above=0.25)
_ = check_operator(classify, out["clean"])
print(f"contract OK; config = {classify.get_config()}")

clean: GeoTensor = out["clean"]  # (1000, 1000) float64 · NaN = dropped
labels: GeoTensor = classify(clean)  # (1000, 1000) float64 → (1000, 1000) uint8
names: dict[int, str] = {0: "no data", 1: "water", 2: "sparse", 3: "vegetation"}
values, counts = np.unique(np.asarray(labels), return_counts=True)
print(
    {
        names[int(v)]: f"{c / counts.sum():.1%}"
        for v, c in zip(values, counts, strict=True)
    }
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
im = ax.imshow(
    np.asarray(labels), cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=3, interpolation="nearest"
)
cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, ticks=list(names))
cbar.ax.set_yticklabels(list(names.values()))
ax.set_title("NDVIClasses on the masked NDVI")
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()
    classify: NDVIClasses = NDVIClasses(water_below=0.02, vegetation_above=0.25) _ = check_operator(classify, out["clean"]) print(f"contract OK; config = {classify.get_config()}") clean: GeoTensor = out["clean"] # (1000, 1000) float64 · NaN = dropped labels: GeoTensor = classify(clean) # (1000, 1000) float64 → (1000, 1000) uint8 names: dict[int, str] = {0: "no data", 1: "water", 2: "sparse", 3: "vegetation"} values, counts = np.unique(np.asarray(labels), return_counts=True) print( { names[int(v)]: f"{c / counts.sum():.1%}" for v, c in zip(values, counts, strict=True) } ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5)) im = ax.imshow( np.asarray(labels), cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=3, interpolation="nearest" ) cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, ticks=list(names)) cbar.ax.set_yticklabels(list(names.values())) ax.set_title("NDVIClasses on the masked NDVI") ax.set_xticks([]) ax.set_yticks([]) plt.show()
    contract OK; config = {'water_below': 0.02, 'vegetation_above': 0.25}
{'no data': '2.7%', 'water': '33.5%', 'sparse': '15.3%', 'vegetation': '48.5%'}

    Summary¶

    • | chained SelectBands, DNToReflectance and NDVI into one Sequential.
    • S2SCL built a drop mask (True = drop) and ApplyMask wrote NaN into it.
    • A Graph joined the NDVI and mask branches; Fanout added NDWI from the same input.
    • NDVIClasses kept the operator contract, and check_operator proved it.

    Next: run this pipeline tile by tile over the whole lake with the patcher, as in the cut notebook. For runtime branching, see Branching pipelines.
